links.outcome: Readability indices and patient-reported understandability of LLM-simplified versus original radiology reports
links.effect: FKGL 5.9 vs 11.0; Reading Ease 71.0 vs 28.2; ease of understanding 4.2 vs 2.6 (Bonferroni P=.02); difficulty with medical terms 2.0 vs 3.6 (Bonferroni P=.04)
links.quote: Supplemental NLP-modified radiology reports were associated with improved objective readability and higher patient-reported perceived ease of understanding in a spine surgery initial consultation setting.

links.outcome: Patient-reported ease of understanding report language and difficulty with medical terms
links.effect: NLP-modified versus original reports: understanding, 4.2 ± 1.2 vs 2.6 ± 1.5 (Bonferroni-corrected-P = .02); medical-term difficulty, 2.0 ± 1.5 vs 3.6 ± 1.4 (Bonferroni-corrected-P = .04).
links.quote: Of 42 survey respondents, those receiving supplemental NLP-modified reports reported greater ease of understanding the report language (4.2 ± 1.2 vs 2.6 ± 1.5, mean-difference 95% CI: 0.75-2.53, P < .01, Bonferroni-corrected-P = .02), and less difficulty with medical terms (2.0 ± 1.5 vs 3.6 ± 1.4, mean-difference 95% CI: -2.51 to -0.60, P < .01, Bonferroni-corrected-P = .04).

links.outcome: Objective readability of supplemental NLP-modified versus original radiology reports
links.effect: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level: 5.9 ± 1.1 vs 11.0 ± 1.7; Reading Ease: 71.0 ± 10.3 vs 28.2 ± 12.5. All four readability indices improved (all P < .01).
links.quote: Among 52 randomized participants (26 women [50%]), NLP-modified reports demonstrated significantly improved objective readability across all indices compared with original reports (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, 5.9 ± 1.1 vs 11.0 ± 1.7; Reading Ease, 71.0 ± 10.3 vs 28.2 ± 12.5; Simple Measure of Gobbledygook, 20.1 ± 12.7 vs 23.5 ± 15.7; Gunning-Fog Index, 8.2 ± 1.1 vs 14.3 ± 1.8; all P < .01).

links.effect: NLP-modified reports led to greater ease of understanding (4.2 vs 2.6) and less difficulty with medical terms (2.0 vs 3.6) compared to original reports.
links.quote: Of 42 survey respondents, those receiving supplemental NLP-modified reports reported greater ease of understanding the report language (4.2 ± 1.2 vs 2.6 ± 1.5, mean-difference 95% CI: 0.75-2.53, P < .01, Bonferroni-corrected-P = .02), and less difficulty with medical terms (2.0 ± 1.5 vs 3.6 ± 1.4, mean-difference 95% CI: -2.51 to -0.60, P < .01, Bonferroni-corrected-P = .04).

screen.practice: supplemental LLM-simplified reports with investigator accuracy review
screen.reason: The study is a prospective randomized controlled trial evaluating the deployment of LLM-simplified radiology reports provided to actual patients. However, it tests the efficacy of the LLM tool/intervention itself against standard care (original reports), rather than comparing different deployment practices or safeguards.
